history.dynasty: Unknown - folk gramadevata tradition, no documented dynastic origin
history.summary: Ankamma Thalli is a Gramadevata (village goddess) worshipped in the Shakta folk tradition around Guntur. Identity is ambiguous: several shrines named Ankamma Thalli exist in/around Guntur (Old Guntur, Nallapadu Rd/NGO Colony, Kolakaluru, Takkellapadu). The documented referent here is the Sri Korlapati Ankamma Ammavari Devasthanam at Christian Pet, Old Guntur, the best-rated listing for this name. Verify the intended shrine with the CSV maintainer.

name: Ankamma Thalli Temple
town_description: Guntur is a major city in coastal Andhra Pradesh and one of the state's key commercial hubs, famed for its chilli markets, cotton trade and tobacco exports. It sits close to Amaravati, the state capital region, and carries ancient history from Buddhist sites at Amaravati and Kondaveedu fort to its colonial-era institutions.

travel.railway: Guntur Junction (~3 km from Old Guntur)
travel.road: City roads and APSRTC buses connect Old Guntur to Guntur Junction and the rest of the city

visitor_information.best_time: Throughout the year; October-February is most comfortable
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 PM per the Justdial listing for the Old Guntur temple; hours differ at other Ankamma shrines - verify
